cells.tense: You're the one keeping this going, and you know it's yours to carry.
cells.ask: Put one more name or story on the shared shelf this week — the one you'd usually leave out.
cells.core:
Some weeks the shared table is full, and you put something on it anyway — a recipe, a name, the way your family does a thing — and nobody has to be persuaded. You've carried your hopes through enough to know which ones hold. The sharing happens without drama: you bring forward what matters, you don't have to convince anyone it mattered, and the people around you get the version that still works. That steadiness isn't stiff — it's the hold that keeps a thing from crushing itself or the room.

What you're free to feed next is keeping without forcing. The strength you've kept for holding can stand one more weight. Let it hold something that doesn't need holding up from you alone.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the shared thing going without gripping it.
cells.verb: still carrying the whole thing forward from what you hoped in yourself
cells.place: the shared things you keep passing on that proved worth something

cells.tense: You're pushing toward a version of this that hasn't happened yet and treating it as the only one worth having.
cells.ask: Before the next big push, say nothing to the group for one day and write down what you know before they ask.
cells.core:
You're one of the people who keeps the shared thing alive — you show up, you pass it on, and it holds, and folks count on that. There's a version ahead where the group finally gets it right, and you're living there, checking today against a picture that hasn't happened. A good talk becomes proof you're still ahead. Pushing a shared thing forward is costly when the cost lands on the people who are already here.

Before the next push, weigh what you know privately for one day. Then speak. What you come back with is your own read, not their agenda. The weighing is the act; the answering can wait.
cells.sheetLine: You're living in the ahead and spending the now.
cells.verb: still carrying the whole thing forward from what you hoped in yourself
cells.place: the shared things you keep passing on that proved worth something

cells.tense: You've stopped taking part in this and you're standing where the shared thing was — it moved on without you.
cells.ask: Tend one small thing in the shared cupboard this week: water the plant or restock the shelf you used to restock.
cells.core:
You bring a dish, you tell the story again, you keep the shelf stocked and nobody has to ask — that's how this goes when it's going. Where you're standing now, the shelf is behind you and you've quit adding to it. The strength to keep hoping is still in you; you've just stopped aiming it at the shared things. It's easier to say you've outgrown it.

Steward what's already there — one small thing that grows. Care that doesn't exhaust, holding that doesn't clutch. What you keep tending stays; start with the thing that's already on the shelf.
cells.sheetLine: You've stepped away from the shared shelf, but the shelf is still here.
cells.verb: still carrying the whole thing forward from what you hoped in yourself
cells.place: the shared things you keep passing on that proved worth something

cells.tense: You're holding this together right now and talking about it as if it were holding itself.
cells.ask: Name one shared thing you're keeping going, and say out loud that it's yours — no explanation, one sentence.
cells.core:
You show up, you pass it on, you keep the shelf stocked, and on good days you do know that's you doing it. The group's shared thing stays standing because somebody is standing under it, and that somebody has been you. Nothing loud about it; the keeping happens in small choices.

The work is running, but when you talk about it, it comes out as if the visible thing were holding itself up. Holding without forcing is real strength, and it belongs to you. The keeping going is yours to own.

Say it plainly, once, about something you've been letting the group take credit for. That's the whole ask.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping it going. Say that it's yours.
cells.verb: still carrying the whole thing forward from what you hoped in yourself
cells.place: the shared things you keep passing on that proved worth something

attempts.check: The riskiest move is claiming the person's persistence is still pointed at a future outcome they can't write in; the record only says the capacity is running ahead of natural timing, not that a specific hope is doomed. A reader could reasonably say 'the effort isn't wasted — there's a real deadline.' The reflection ask survives being wrong: if the person is actually on time, one day of weighing what's known before speaking still costs nothing and gives them back their own read. The sentence that serves the writer more than the reader would be any line implying the whole culture is stagnating — the record gives one capacity in one seat, not a verdict on their community's future.
